chapters.title: A foothold
chapters.text: Around the year 1250, our ships leave the Weser marshes for a rumored island off the Frisian coast. A gale separates the ships. Twelve families wait with Skipper Elin while we find a safe harbor. Grow the first harvest and light the way home.
chapters.hint: Build a farm, add a pond or river beside it, then collect 30 food. A farm waters its own patch at first; fresh water keeps it productive.

chapters.title: Put down roots
chapters.text: We carried a carved roof beam from our old hall across the sea. I want our children to build their own. Tend this woodland, grow new trees, and cut only what the settlement can replace.
chapters.hint: Prepare rich soil, plant three trees, and water them. Most trees need about two wet days to mature. Collect 20 timber from a nearby sawpit.

chapters.title: A place to belong
chapters.text: Elin’s sail is on the horizon. We can still return east—or make a promise here. Raise homes around a market, where strangers can become neighbors and every family has a place.
chapters.hint: Build three cottages and a market. A quarry near boulders or a mountain will provide the 15 stone we need.

chapters.title: The lost fleet returns
chapters.text: The fleet survived, but the northern gales are coming. On Day 30 I will attempt the passage. Let the waiting families see smoke from their own hearths—and food enough to believe they can stay.
chapters.hint: Stock the harbor with 60 food, 20 timber, and 15 stone. Keep three safe cottages and three healthy mature trees. The fleet sails as soon as everything is ready, from Day 12, and no later than Day 30.

chapters.title: A harvest worth keeping
chapters.text: Twelve settlers have stepped ashore. Elin saved the old hall’s carved beam; now we must earn the right to raise it. Food is no longer only a trade good: every family eats daily, and winter hearths consume timber. Build a granary and keep a reserve.
chapters.hint: Wonders is the second tab in Build. The granary needs gold, food, timber, and stone together. It doubles every building’s storage.

chapters.title: A watch above the harbor
chapters.text: A trader brings welcome news of the lost fleet—and a warning. The Red Sail crews have begun taking cargo from isolated harbors. Lay roads, welcome the next families, and raise a watchtower so no ship arrives unseen.
chapters.hint: Complete a watchtower (Build → Defense filter), five cottages and two farms. Paint roads near workshops for a production bonus; any road tier counts.

chapters.title: Bread on the wind
chapters.text: The first winter taught us to keep more than one source of food. Let the wind grind grain while orchards ripen. I have saved seeds from the crossing; plant them where our grandchildren will gather fruit.
chapters.hint: Complete a windmill; its 25% farm bonus applies across the island. Plant fruit trees on watered, fertile land.

chapters.title: A place at the table
chapters.text: Two strangers from a storm-damaged ship ask for shelter. Some fear another mouth to feed. I ask the council to remember our own crossing. Make room for them, and train a small harbor watch to protect everyone who stays.
chapters.hint: Complete a guard hall and train two guards in Army. Six safe cottages provide 24 beds. Deliver goods with the journal button; each chapter starts a new delivery.

chapters.title: The forest covenant
chapters.text: The Red Sails burn their winter driftwood to patch their ships. We can build a different future: a living forest that gives timber year after year. At the council stone, promise to plant more kinds than we cut.
chapters.hint: Keep six mature healthy trees from three species. Give both sawpits trees within five tiles.

chapters.title: The river does the work
chapters.text: A thaw swells the river. The same water that threatens the stores can turn a wheel all summer. Build with the island, and its strength becomes ours.
chapters.hint: Watermills need fresh water within four tiles. Ponds and rivers count; the sea does not.

chapters.title: Life beneath the surface
chapters.text: One of Elin’s missing boats returns with news: other crews survived farther west. Keep our bay alive, so a failed harvest need not become an empty table. Fish and fields together give the fleet a reason to reunite.
chapters.hint: Two fishing docks need clean water. Fish and ducks survive around ponds; meadow animals need food nearby.

chapters.title: An open port
chapters.text: The Red Sail captain demands a share of our cargo. Elin refuses. An open harbor needs a strong watch as well as honest scales. Reach 20 defense, welcome our allies, and prove that trade can prosper without tribute.
chapters.hint: Build the harbor near water. It increases sale prices by 25%. The trade goal counts gold earned by selling goods, not charter income.

chapters.title: A garden within walls
chapters.text: Elin returns with seeds and a lay brother who knows how walls hold the sun’s warmth. The old world is not only a place we lost; it is knowledge we can carry forward. Give that knowledge a home before the next frost.
chapters.hint: The cloister garden increases orchard food by 50%. Grow six healthy tree species and six mature fruit-bearing plants.

chapters.title: The smallest workers
chapters.text: A child asks why the orchard has flowers but little fruit. The answer is smaller than any ship: bees and butterflies. Keep their meadows, and the island will feed those who cannot yet hold a spade.
chapters.hint: Plant wildflowers, wild cherry, or hawthorn. Place pollinators close to flowers and keep the habitat watered.

chapters.title: The dark tide
chapters.text: A damaged cog drifts into the bay. Its spilled whale oil stains the shore we promised to protect. The council can blame the sea—or repair the harm. Find the spill and restore every affected patch.
chapters.hint: Use Locate spill, then Restore → Clean-up over the entire marked patch. Treat all affected tiles; clean soil has oil below 5% and taint below 15%.

chapters.title: A light in the storm
chapters.text: I hear a bell in the fog, then nothing. We cannot ask families to cross this ocean without a light to guide them. Raise the lighthouse; its beam will be a promise that this harbor stays open in bad weather.
chapters.hint: The lighthouse reduces the storm production penalty to 10%. Prepare ten safe cottages for the next arrivals.

chapters.title: A map of the stars
chapters.text: Our children no longer ask when we are going home. They ask what lies beyond our sea. Build a scriptorium to copy the star tables, so the next crossing begins with knowledge instead of desperation.
chapters.hint: A scriptorium earns income from copied books and adds 4 daily charter gold. Lay 30 cobblestone tiles through the town.

chapters.title: Four days without rain
chapters.text: Four days without rain. The council’s weather-lore was right, but foresight only matters if we act. Spread fresh water through the fields and woodland; show the younger settlers that preparation is stronger than fear.
chapters.hint: This chapter begins with four dry days, then rain returns. Expand fresh water to 45 tiles and keep 12 trees healthy through it.

chapters.title: Goods from every shore
chapters.text: Three neighboring crews offer a covenant: mutual trade and relief when one shore suffers. Fill their holds fairly. One day we may need their kindness as much as their gold.
chapters.hint: Decide the market charter in the journal; the choice lasts for the rest of the game. Then trade food, timber or stone, keeping enough for the delivery.

chapters.title: The guilds of Haven
chapters.text: The old carved beam has waited beside my hearth since the crossing. Today we will lift it into a common hall. Reach 32 defense and let every craft, every crew, and every family have a voice beneath its roof.
chapters.hint: The guildhall speeds construction by 25%. Thirteen safe cottages house 52 residents.

chapters.title: A patchwork of habitats
chapters.text: The settlement spreads toward the last meadow. I ask the council to leave room for lives other than our own. A haven is not complete until the river, forest, and smallest creatures can thrive here too.
chapters.hint: Grow ten mature tree species. Maintain six animal species with food, flowers, clean water, and enough room.

chapters.title: The great storm tide
chapters.text: The old fishermen read a great storm tide in the sky. This time the fleet is already in our harbor. For four days, every beam, storehouse, and promise we made will be tested. Keep the light burning and prepare relief cargo.
chapters.hint: Four storm days start this chapter. Keep the lighthouse working, then deliver the relief cargo. Preparedness protects progress; there is no forced purchase.

chapters.title: The island gives back
chapters.text: Beyond the storm, a neighboring settlement has lost its stores. Once we waited for someone to come back for us. Now we are the ship on their horizon. Send what they need to begin again.
chapters.hint: Deliver a large mixed cargo. Protected deliveries cannot accidentally be sold. Use Auto-collect while your economy works.

chapters.title: A haven for generations
chapters.text: The children gather beneath the carved beam to hear about our first crossing. Outside, 64 people call this island home. Raise a sanctuary, keep a 40-strength watch, and leave a living haven to those who come after us. Our voyage becomes their beginning.
chapters.hint: Build the sanctuary with all four resources, house 64 settlers, and nurture 20 trees. After the ceremony, rotating commissions bring new deliveries and rewards.

chapters.title: Beyond the familiar fields
chapters.text: A scout returns with a map of broad inland valleys. The refuge has survived; now it must learn how to grow without consuming its own future. Establish a second district and send a surveying party.
chapters.hint: Explore the enlarged map. Districts are 24 × 24 tile regions; completed buildings in different regions count.

chapters.title: The inland road
chapters.text: Wagons sink into mud between the new fields and the port. Build a lasting road network before the next harvest, with places to shelter along the route.
chapters.hint: Cobblestones count toward all road goals. Fresh stone collection starts at the beginning of this chapter.

chapters.title: Bread for two shores
chapters.text: The inland families have cleared their fields, but their first crop will be late. Keep them fed while a second mill begins turning.
chapters.hint: Build productive farms near water. This harvest must be collected during this chapter.

chapters.title: The charter of the valleys
chapters.text: The coast and valleys agree to share their stores. It is a promise of work, not a gift of endless coin. Establish a third district and pay for its common works.
chapters.hint: Choose how the stores are shared (journal). The gold delivery pays for roads and common works.

chapters.title: Before the hungry season
chapters.text: Cold winds arrive before the last grain is dry. The council must choose stores over celebration. Build another granary and hold a winter reserve.
chapters.hint: Stored reserves are separate from delivered cargo. Feed the settlers after you have made the delivery.

chapters.title: Light through the frost
chapters.text: The youngest settlers have never seen a winter without fear. Show them that preparation can outlast it. Keep morale high while gathering a new harvest within walls.
chapters.hint: Cloister gardens and fisheries diversify food production when farms slow in winter.

chapters.title: The timber bargain
chapters.text: A shipbuilder offers tools in exchange for timber. Accept only what the forest can replace. Raise a third sawpit and keep a diverse canopy.
chapters.hint: Answer the shipbuilder in the journal. Healthy mature trees must remain while you produce and deliver new timber.

chapters.title: No hearth left cold
chapters.text: Families from the windward shore request shelter. A larger town means a larger responsibility at every dawn. Prepare homes and supplies before welcoming them.
chapters.hint: Ninety-six settlers need 24 safe cottages. Steady harvests matter more than a full store: keep Auto-collect on and farms watered.

goals.label: Food harvested each day, 3 days running

chapters.title: Red sails return
chapters.text: The rival captain has gathered new ships. This time he wants the whole harbor. Recruit a visible watch and build the defenses that let peaceful trade continue.
chapters.hint: Answer the Red Sail captain in the journal. Army is the shield tab; Find soldiers shows the trained garrison beside its halls.

goals.label: Council decision: answer to the Red Sails

chapters.title: Keep the channel open
chapters.text: Merchants hesitate at the sight of hostile sails. Show them that a defended harbor is still an open harbor. Earn their trust with fresh trade and food stores.
chapters.hint: Trade earned before this chapter does not count toward this contract.

goals.label: Food harvested each day, 3 days running

chapters.title: The watch holds
chapters.text: A warning bell crosses the water. Let the Red Sails see a town that will neither starve nor yield. Survive two announced threats with a stronger watch.
chapters.hint: The Red Sail fleet strikes first, harder than any raid so far. Form a shield line, keep the watch paid and the stores full.

chapters.title: An independent harbor
chapters.text: The rival captain offers a truce. We will accept peace, but not tribute. Send relief to a neighboring shore and demonstrate that strength can protect generosity.
chapters.hint: Keep three guard halls and twelve soldiers; defense buildings provide the remaining strength.

chapters.title: A council beyond the coast
chapters.text: Delegates arrive from four shores. Each brings a different need, and each deserves a voice. Expand into a fourth district and give the delegates a common hall.
chapters.hint: Seat the council (journal). Plan a neighborhood: cottages within six tiles of a well, a market and a chapel earn more rent and count here.

goals.label: Council decision: who sits at the council
Homes with a well, market and chapel close by

chapters.title: The river workshops
chapters.text: The inland river can turn more than one wheel. Its workshops will supply the coast while the forest recovers. Build a second watermill and quarry.
chapters.hint: Watermills require fresh water; quarries need stone nearby. Five different workshops must be producing at once, so keep their inputs supplied.

chapters.title: An honest measure
chapters.text: The council agrees on fair weights. Every market must earn its place by serving families, and every shipment must leave the island able to feed itself.
chapters.hint: Reach 3,000 new trade gold while the harvest stays steady. Selling a lot at once lowers prices for a few days; spread sales out.

goals.label: Food harvested each day, 3 days running

chapters.title: The common store
chapters.text: The island can no longer depend on a single harvest or storehouse. Build a reserve that belongs to every district, and welcome the next generation.
chapters.hint: Population rises only when you complete the chapter. Prepare enough food production for the new daily demand.

goals.label: Homes with a well, market and chapel close by

chapters.title: The summer of dry wells
chapters.text: The first dry wells are a warning. Carry water to the farms now, while the rivers still run. Keep your woodland alive through the dry season.
chapters.hint: Settle the water rights in the journal. Fresh water irrigates nearby ground; keep a living canopy through the dry spell.

chapters.title: The great harbor repair
chapters.text: A season of storms has scarred the docks. Repair the trading fleet before isolation becomes hunger. Endure two further threats and keep both lights working.
chapters.hint: Natural events continue throughout the work. Granaries, lights and firewood reduce losses.

chapters.title: The winter council
chapters.text: The council meets with no feast before it. This year, the measure of prosperity is what remains in the stores after everyone has eaten.
chapters.hint: Choose the winter law (journal). Then complete the delivery and hold both reserves without a single short dawn.

chapters.title: A watch for every shore
chapters.text: The youngest guard was born here. For her, the island is not a refuge from another life; it is home. Give every district the protection its families deserve.
chapters.hint: Red Sails strike at the start of this chapter. Eighteen soldiers is the full watch; towers, palisades and beacons add the rest.

chapters.title: The living commons
chapters.text: The council marks the common woods: no family may claim the river or the last meadow. Keep room for creatures whose lives sustain our own.
chapters.hint: Keep a broad canopy and several habitats. Add animals near food and clean water shortly before claiming the chapter.

chapters.title: Letters from the next coast
chapters.text: A letter arrives from a settlement that once asked for our help. They now offer ships for a joint expedition. Fund the voyage with new trade, not old promises.
chapters.hint: This chapter needs 5,000 trade gold earned after it begins, plus its own protected shipment.

chapters.title: The long promise
chapters.text: We cannot promise our children gentle weather. We can leave them homes, knowledge, and a council that prepares. Build a second sanctuary and make room for 160 people.
chapters.hint: Make the last great choice in the journal. All special buildings still require all four resources.

goals.label: Council decision: what we leave behind

chapters.title: A realm worth keeping
chapters.text: The carved beam stands above a room full of children. Beyond it are five thriving districts, a living forest, and a harbor open to strangers. The next chapter belongs to them. Prove that the realm can sustain the promise.
chapters.hint: The last Red Sail assault comes first. Resolve two threats, fund the final common-works shipment and get through eight dawns without a shortage. Commissions follow.

council.title: The market charter
council.prompt: The neighboring crews will trade with us, but on whose terms? The guilds want a charter; the boat crews want open scales.

a.title: Open scales
a.effect: Sale prices +10%, and buyers absorb 50% more before prices dip.

b.title: A guild charter
b.effect: Workshops produce 15% more; each working workshop pays 1 gold a day in dues.

council.title: Sharing the stores
council.prompt: Coast and valleys must agree how grain is kept. One common granary, or every family its own plot and loft?

a.title: One common granary
a.effect: Food spoils half as fast above your reserve; settlers eat 10% more as rations are shared out.

council.title: The shipbuilder’s offer
council.prompt: The shipbuilder offers iron saws and wedges for our timber. Faster work, but the woods will feel it.

a.title: Take the tools
a.effect: Sawpits and quarries produce 25% more; morale recovers 1 point a day slower.

b.title: Keep the old ways
b.effect: Trees grow 25% faster and wild animals move in twice as often.

council.title: Answer to the Red Sails
council.prompt: The Red Sail captain offers to spare us for a yearly toll. Do we pay, or build walls?

a.title: Raise the walls
a.effect: Watchtowers, palisades and beacons give 50% more defense; wary merchants pay 8% less.

b.title: Pay the toll
b.effect: Raids come 25% weaker; the toll costs 2 gold a day from the charter.

council.title: Who sits at the council
council.prompt: The delegates ask who should hold the seats: the master craftsmen, or one elder from every family?

b.title: The families
b.effect: Morale never drops below 80, so production never falls below 80%.

council.title: Water rights
council.prompt: The wells are failing. Dig deep wells for the fields, or dike the marsh for fish ponds?

a.title: Deep wells
a.effect: Farms never lose more than 20% to dry soil or drought.

b.title: Dike the marsh
b.effect: Fisheries and piers produce 30% more food.

council.title: The winter law
council.prompt: This winter the stores must last. Strict rations, or open hearths so nobody sits in the cold?

a.title: Strict rations
a.effect: Settlers eat 20% less; morale recovers half as fast.

b.title: Open hearths
b.effect: Winter firewood use rises 50%; morale recovers 2 points a day faster.

council.title: What we leave behind
council.prompt: The charter allows one last great work. A school for the children, or an infirmary for the hard years?

a.title: A school
a.effect: The charter pays 4 more gold every day.

b.title: An infirmary
b.effect: Every storm, frost, flood or raid takes 25% less.

water.name: Fresh water
water.description: Soaks a patch of land. Seeds need moisture to grow.

soil.name: Rich soil
soil.description: Adds fertile soil to the bare sand. A good place to start.

compost.name: Compost
compost.description: Feeds the soil and helps existing plants grow faster.

pond.name: Pond
pond.description: Makes lasting freshwater habitat for fish and ducks.

sand.name: Sand
sand.description: Creates a dry sandy patch with little nutrition.

rock.name: Boulders
rock.description: Adds a cluster of stones. Plants cannot grow on rock.

grass.name: Meadow grass
grass.description: Quick-growing ground cover. Spreads slowly when healthy.

clover.name: Clover
clover.description: A low meadow plant that gradually improves soil.

flowers.name: Wildflowers
flowers.description: Grows into flowers that support bees and butterflies.

oak.name: Oak seeds
oak.description: Small seedlings become tall trees over several island days.

pine.name: Scots pine seeds
pine.description: Slow-growing trees that tolerate colder weather.

fern.name: Ferns
fern.description: Thrives in wet ground. Struggles during drought.

berry.name: Berry bush
berry.description: Grows into food for grazing animals.

mushroom.name: Mushrooms
mushroom.description: Likes damp, fertile ground and replenishes the soil.

rabbit.name: Rabbits
rabbit.description: Grazes on grass and clover. Needs a living patch of meadow. Arrives as a family of 3.

deer.name: Deer
deer.description: Browses shrubs and meadow plants. Needs plenty of vegetation.

fox.name: Foxes
fox.description: Roams the island and hunts rabbits. Add prey first.

sheep.name: Sheep
sheep.description: Grazes on meadow plants, leaving room for new shoots. Arrives as a family of 2.

duck.name: Ducks
duck.description: Feels at home beside a pond. Wanders and swims. Arrives as a family of 3.

fish.name: Fish
fish.description: Lives in ponds, rivers, and ocean water. Needs clean water and cannot live on dry land. Arrives as a family of 3.

butterfly.name: Butterflies
butterfly.description: Pollinates flowering plants. Needs nearby flowers. Arrives as a family of 2.

bee.name: Bees
bee.description: Helps nearby plants grow. Depends on a flowering habitat. Arrives as a family of 3.

boar.name: Wild boar
boar.description: Roots through woodland for acorns, berries and fungi. Needs trees and shrubs close by. Arrives as a pair.

squirrel.name: Red squirrels
squirrel.description: Lives among mature trees. Needs a wood of grown trees nearby. Arrives as a pair.

hedgehog.name: Hedgehogs
hedgehog.description: Forages hedges and meadow edges at dusk. Needs low plants around it. Arrives as a pair.

stork.name: White storks
stork.description: Stalks wet meadows for frogs. Needs water within a short walk. Arrives as a pair.

heron.name: Grey heron
heron.description: Stands patiently at the water’s edge. Needs a pond, river or shore beside it.

otter.name: Otters
otter.description: Hunts along clean rivers and ponds. Needs water beside it. Arrives as a pair.

cow.name: Cattle
cow.description: Hardy marsh cattle graze open meadow. Needs plenty of grass. Arrives as a pair.

goose.name: Greylag geese
goose.description: Grazes by ponds and rivers. Needs water close by. Arrives as a family of 3.

oil.name: Whale-oil spill
oil.description: Leaves a dark slick, contaminates soil, and spreads in wet weather.

gasoline.name: Pitch
gasoline.description: Smothers plants and leaves flammable pitch. Storms may ignite it.

nuclear.name: Tanner’s vat
nuclear.description: Adds a tanner’s vat that steadily fouls nearby ground.

acid.name: Lye
acid.description: Damages plants and animals and degrades the soil.

trash.name: Refuse
trash.description: Clutters the ground and reduces habitat quality.

fire.name: Spark
fire.description: Starts a small fire where fuel or dry plants can burn.

cleanup.name: Clean-up
cleanup.description: Removes spills, refuse, and tanner’s vats. The taint fades slowly.

biochar.name: Wood ash
biochar.description: Reduces soil contamination and restores fertility.

erase.name: Clear patch
erase.description: Removes added plants, animals, and objects from a small patch.

river.name: River
river.description: Draw a freshwater channel. Irrigates nearby ground. Price per brush section.

ocean.name: Ocean
ocean.description: Carve an inlet or sea into the island. Saltwater does not irrigate crops. Price per section.

land.name: Reclaim land
land.description: Raise dry land from water. Connect islands or fill an inlet. Price per section.

mountain.name: Mountain
mountain.description: Raise a rocky peak. Nearby quarries can produce stone.

snowpeak.name: Frosted crag
snowpeak.description: Raise a high crag that holds the winter frost. Provides stone for nearby quarries.

hill.name: Hill
hill.description: Raise a grassy terrace. Adds real elevation to the landscape.

road.name: Stone road
road.description: Paint a road through your settlement. Nearby roads improve building production by 15%. Price per section.

path.name: Dirt path
path.description: Paint a simple path. Buildings within 2.5 tiles produce 5% more. Costs 1 gold per tile.

paved.name: Cobblestone
paved.description: A finished village street. Buildings within 2.5 tiles produce 25% more. Upgrades cost only the difference.

remove_road.name: Remove road
remove_road.description: Remove one road tile for 1 gold. Buildings and plants stay in place.

hazel.name: Hazel shrub
hazel.description: A rounded woodland shrub. Adds a low layer beneath taller trees.

juniper.name: Blue juniper
juniper.description: A low evergreen shrub that tolerates dry soil and cold weather.

heather.name: Heather
heather.description: Magenta flowers that feed pollinators. Tolerates drier ground.

lupine.name: Loosestrife
lupine.description: Violet flower spikes for sunny, moist meadows. Supports bees.

reeds.name: Cattail reeds
reeds.description: Plant in fresh water or wet ground along a pond or river. Saltwater is unsuitable.

sedge.name: Golden sedge
sedge.description: Golden tussocks for damp riverbanks and shallow fresh water.

bluebells.name: Bluebells
bluebells.description: Blue woodland flowers. Likes damp soil and supports pollinators.

bracken.name: Bracken fern
bracken.description: A spreading copper-green fern. Needs damp, fertile woodland soil.

birch.name: Silver birch
birch.description: An airy white-barked tree for a bright northern woodland.

maple.name: Field maple
maple.description: A compact European maple with golden autumn foliage.

willow.name: White willow
willow.description: A graceful riverbank tree. Needs plenty of moisture.

beech.name: European beech
beech.description: A broad woodland canopy with smooth silver-grey bark.

alder.name: Black alder
alder.description: A dark green tree for damp riverbanks. Plant beside fresh water.

hornbeam.name: Hornbeam
hornbeam.description: A compact, dense-crowned woodland tree. Excellent sawpit timber.

rowan.name: Rowan
rowan.description: An airy tree with red berries, suited to cool woodland edges.

spruce.name: Norway spruce
spruce.description: A layered evergreen for cooler uplands. Tolerates snow.

yew.name: European yew
yew.description: A dense dark evergreen. Tolerates shade and drier soil.

hawthorn.name: Hawthorn
hawthorn.description: A small flowering tree at the meadow edge. Supports pollinators.

apple.name: Apple tree
apple.description: A village orchard tree. Mature trees contribute food to the harvest.

pear.name: Pear tree
pear.description: An upright orchard tree. Mature trees contribute food to the harvest.

plum.name: Plum tree
plum.description: A rounded orchard tree with purple fruit. Mature trees produce food.

cherry_tree.name: Wild cherry
cherry_tree.description: Pale spring blossom supports pollinators; mature trees produce food.

farm.name: Wheat farm
farm.description: Produces up to 40 food/day. Fertile, wet ground and nearby rivers improve harvests.

sawmill.name: Sawpit
sawmill.description: Produces up to 24 timber/day near mature trees. Protect the forest to keep the sawpit productive.

quarry.name: Stone quarry
quarry.description: Produces 20 stone/day near a mountain, alpine peak, or boulders.

fishery.name: Fishing dock
fishery.description: Produces 30 food/day beside a river, pond, or coast. Needs clean water.

market.name: Market square
market.description: Earns 2 gold/day, plus 0.7 for each nearby cottage.

cottage.name: Cottage
cottage.description: Houses four residents and earns 0.8 gold/day. Residents improve nearby markets.

granary.name: Great granary
granary.description: Doubles building storage to 600, adds 1,500 food reserve capacity and produces 12 food/day. Keep harvests safe between visits.

windmill.name: Hilltop windmill
windmill.description: All farms produce 25% more. Mills flour worth 15 food/day. Farm bonuses do not stack.

watermill.name: River watermill
watermill.description: Produces 18 timber/day beside fresh water. Needs a pond or river within four tiles.

harbor.name: Merchant harbor
harbor.description: Trade sales earn 25% more; produces 6 gold/day. Needs water within four tiles. Trade bonuses do not stack.

glasshouse.name: Cloister garden
glasshouse.description: Produces 25 food/day. Mature orchards yield 50% more fruit, even through changing seasons.

lighthouse.name: Wayfarer lighthouse
lighthouse.description: Reduces the island-wide storm production penalty from 40% to 10%. Generates 3 gold/day.

observatory.name: Starfall scriptorium
observatory.description: Adds 4 charter gold/day, plus 5 gold/day from copied books. Opens the expedition’s final age.

guildhall.name: Guildhall of Haven
guildhall.description: Produces 10 gold/day. Construction of every new building runs 25% faster.

sanctuary.name: Sanctuary of the tides
sanctuary.description: The island’s great wonder. Cleanses tainted ground near it, nurtures nearby plants, and earns 12 gold/day.

watchtower.name: Watchtower
watchtower.description: Adds 6 defense. A completed tower gives four days of warning before the next threat, instead of three.

palisade.name: Palisade gate
palisade.description: Adds 4 settlement defense. A shared defensive perimeter protects the whole island; road connections are not required.

guardhall.name: Guard hall
guardhall.description: Provides room for six guards. Train pairs in Army. Each guard adds 3 defense and needs food and gold daily.

bakery.name: Village bakery
bakery.description: Bakes 34 food/day, using 2 timber/day. Keep fuel collected.

well.name: Village well
well.description: Keeps soil within four tiles watered, even through drought.

herbalist.name: Herbalist cottage
herbalist.description: Produces 22 food/day from a mature woodland site.

storehouse.name: Supply storehouse
storehouse.description: Adds 800 to the island food reserve before spoilage.

carpenter.name: Carpenter workshop
carpenter.description: Produces 14 timber/day beside mature woodland; uses 3 food/day.

stonemason.name: Stonemason yard
stonemason.description: Produces 12 stone/day; uses 2 timber and 2 food/day.

smithy.name: Blacksmith forge
smithy.description: Produces 24 gold/day using 2 timber and 1 stone/day.

stables.name: Village stables
stables.description: Produces 18 gold/day from carting, using 2 food/day.

chapel.name: Harbor chapel
chapel.description: A completed chapel restores 2 extra morale per day when supplied.

bathhouse.name: Bathhouse
bathhouse.description: Produces 20 gold/day; needs nearby water and 1 timber/day.

apiary.name: Meadow apiary
apiary.description: Produces 24 food/day beside healthy flowering plants.

shipyard.name: Boatbuilders’ yard
shipyard.description: Produces 36 gold/day using 3 timber/day. Needs nearby water.

beacon.name: Signal beacon
beacon.description: Adds 8 settlement defense and extends threat warnings.

garden.name: Kitchen garden
garden.description: Produces 18 food/day, falling to 6 in winter.

pier.name: Riverside pier
pier.description: Produces 20 food/day beside a river, pond or coast.

timber_bridge.name: Timber bridge
timber_bridge.description: Span a river between two clear banks. 20 gold + 8 timber per section. Tap water, Turn to align, then confirm the full cost.

stone_bridge.name: Stone bridge
stone_bridge.description: A stone crossing with cobbled approaches. 30 gold + 4 timber + 8 stone per section. Up to 12 water tiles; takes longer to build.

remove_bridge.name: Remove bridge
remove_bridge.description: Tap a crossing to remove the whole bridge. Unfinished work returns 50% of its resources; completed bridges have no refund.
